# 2026.320.0528 — fix(k3s): the auto-generated cluster token is 44-char url-safe base64, and two stale citations go

## Summary

Head `282c18994123672564bfbe3fb98fb909cce78e61`, based on `origin/main` (0 behind, 1 ahead):
` 2 files changed, 7 insertions(+), 5 deletions(-)` — `.agents/skills/k3s-server/SKILL.md` and `charly.yml`.

`K3S_CLUSTER_TOKEN` is shared between `k3s-server` and `k3s-agent`: whichever resolves the
`secret_require:` first generates it, and the other reads the persisted value. Two surfaces described that
generated token wrongly, and one surface cited code that no longer exists:

| surface | said | truth |
|---|---|---|
| `.agents/skills/k3s-server/SKILL.md` | "a 32-byte hex token" | `deploykit.GenerateRandomSecretToken(32)` — 32 random bytes as **url-safe base64, 44 characters** (Fernet-key compatible) |
| `charly.yml` (the layer comment) | `DefaultCredentialStore.Set` and `charly/layer_secrets.go` / `ensureLayerSecret` | that symbol is gone (`sdk/deploykit` records its removal); the value is persisted by the credential store and read back by the other side |

The override example (`charly secrets set charly/secret/K3S_CLUSTER_TOKEN <value>`, `openssl rand -hex 32`)
is unchanged: that is an operator-chosen value, not the framework's shape.

Part of the claim-keyed sweep tracked by **opencharly/opencharly#1066** — the issue whose first count was
wrong; the corrected table puts this repo among the remaining source surfaces, and this PR closes its row.
